Time-Dependent ROC Curve from a Survival-Probability Matrix

Source: R/roc_survmat.R
roc_survmat.Rd

Computes the full cumulative/dynamic time-dependent ROC curve (sensitivity vs. specificity across risk-score thresholds) at a fixed horizon t_star, using the same inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted (IPCW) case/control definition as auc_survmat (Uno et al. 2007; Heagerty and Zheng 2005). Its trapezoidal AUC closely tracks auc_survmat's pairwise-concordance AUC (small numerical differences arise from tie handling between the step-function ROC curve and the exact pairwise comparison).

Usage

roc_survmat(object, predicted, t_star)

# S3 method for class 'roc_survmat'
plot(x, title, ...)

plot_roc(x, ...)

Arguments

object

A Surv object of length \(n\).

predicted

An n x k matrix or data frame of survival probabilities with columns named "t=<time>".

t_star

Numeric time at which to evaluate the ROC curve.

x

A roc_survmat object.

title

Plot title. If missing, an automatically generated title is used (includes the AUC). Pass NULL to omit the title entirely.

...

Additional arguments passed to plot.roc_survmat.

Value

An object of class "roc_survmat": a list with curve (a data.frame with threshold, sensitivity, specificity), auc, and t_star.

Details

As in auc_survmat, cases are subjects with an observed event strictly before t_star (IPCW-weighted by \(1/\hat G(\tilde T_i)\)), and controls are subjects known to survive beyond t_star. The risk score is \(1 - \hat S(t^\star \mid x)\). Sensitivity and specificity are swept over every observed risk-score value \(c\): $$ \widehat{\mathrm{Se}}(c) = \frac{\sum_{i \in \text{cases}} w_i\, I(\text{risk}_i \ge c)} {\sum_{i \in \text{cases}} w_i}, \qquad \widehat{\mathrm{Sp}}(c) = \frac{\sum_{i \in \text{controls}} I(\text{risk}_i < c)} {|\text{controls}|}. $$

References

Uno H, Cai T, Tian L, Wei LJ (2007). Evaluating prediction rules for t-year survivors with censored regression models. doi:10.1198/016214507000000149

Heagerty PJ, Zheng Y (2005). Survival model predictive accuracy and ROC curves. doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.2005.030814.x

See also

auc_survmat(), plot.roc_survmat()

Examples

y <- survival::Surv(time = veteran$time, event = veteran$status)
sp <- matrix(stats::plogis(scale(veteran$karno)), ncol = 1,
            dimnames = list(NULL, "t=100"))
r <- roc_survmat(y, predicted = sp, t_star = 100)
r$auc
#> [1] 0.7962477
head(r$curve)
#>   threshold sensitivity specificity
#> 1 0.1173737   1.0000000   0.0000000
#> 2 0.1724406   1.0000000   0.0000000
#> 3 0.2109977   1.0000000   0.1320755
#> 4 0.2555142   0.9865336   0.1320755
#> 5 0.3057828   0.9090763   0.4339623
#> 6 0.3611437   0.8962462   0.4528302
